chunks: It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was over the water, so that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed. And if you say, 'You will surely be resurrected after death,' those who disbelieve will say, 'This is nothing but obvious magic.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the creation of the heavens and earth and the test of human deeds?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the phrase 'His Throne was upon the water' (Ibn Abbas) is often interpreted as signifying the primordial element of creation or the divine knowledge preceding the physical universe, highlighting God's absolute sovereignty. This verse underscores the purpose of creation as a test of moral excellence (ihsan), contrasting the tangible reality of resurrection with the skeptics' dismissal of it as 'clear magic,' a theme resonating with the concept of Haqq vs. Batil in Shia theology.
